approach: Newton's law of cooling gives an exponential decay toward the surrounding temperature, so the logarithm of the temperature excess ratio is proportional to time.

steps.text: Write the exponential cooling law with the temperature excess decaying from the surrounding temperature.
Use the first cooling case to find the rate constant k.
Use the second cooling case with the same k to find the unknown time.
steps.why_this_step: The rate constant k depends only on the object and its surroundings, not on the starting temperature, so it carries over from the first case.

steps.text: Solve for t using the value of k found in the first case.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the object cools at a constant rate of 6°C per minute and scaling the 50°C drop proportionally gives about 8.3 min, ignoring that cooling slows near the surrounding temperature.
